title: Event-driven command completion
summary: Add a durable TaskPlane-owned command runtime and canonical adapters so commands wake the model only on meaningful idempotent events, resume without relaunch, aggregate waves, bound output, and enforce wake/token budgets across Claude and Codex.

current_state.summary: TaskPlane has durable run/loop stores, bounded process execution, normalized Claude/Codex outcomes, cancellation/timeout cleanup, and host capability routing. Execution remains caller-blocking or subprocess.run-based; eval_drivers.run_process polls an in-process Popen. No durable command handle, transition journal, reconnect contract, delivery lease, wave authority, or polling-token gate exists.

alternatives.name: Canonical durable command broker
alternatives.description: TaskPlane owns handles, transitions, blocking waits, leases, artifacts, waves and budgets; adapters translate host capabilities.

tradeoffs.revisit_when: Every supported host provides the complete durable, bound, replay-safe, aggregating and observable contract.

alternatives.name: Host-native handles with thin facade
alternatives.description: Persist host identifiers and delegate waiting and summaries.

tradeoffs.revisit_when: Both hosts publish stable equivalent completion/resume APIs and delivery receipts.

alternatives.name: In-memory background extension
alternatives.description: Move current polling to background threads without durable command state.

tradeoffs.revisit_when: Only for explicitly short synchronous commands.

decision: Extend the durable-store and bounded-adapter stack with one TaskPlane-owned lifecycle and host-neutral adapter boundary. Persist before yielding, wake only from meaningful idempotent transitions, keep UI progress out of conversation, and retain synchronous execution as an additive wrapper.

contracts.description: Opaque workspace/auth-bound handle, meaningful events, revisions and idempotent delivery.
Host-neutral launch, wait_next, cancel, reconnect and snapshot with blocking fallback.
Sealed membership, attention policy and one ordinary aggregate completion.
Wake/token telemetry and hard budget evaluation.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC1: A silent command running for at least five minutes causes zero model turns between launch and its first meaningful state change.
acceptance_map.validation: Fake clock advances 300 seconds without events; assert model_delivery_count==0 before terminal transition.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC2: Normal completion causes exactly one model wake-up with a structured result.
acceptance_map.validation: Completion/replay test asserts one delivery with status, exit code, elapsed_ms and bounded delta.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC3: Failure, cancellation, timeout, and approval-needed states each cause exactly one wake-up.
acceptance_map.validation: Parameterized fake-event test asserts one delivery for failed, cancelled, timed_out and approval_required.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC4: Identical or unchanged output is never written into the conversation.
acceptance_map.validation: Repeated identical-output fixture asserts zero conversation records/deliveries until a meaningful event.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC5: Large output is stored once as an artifact; the model receives only a bounded summary and reference.
acceptance_map.design_element: taskplane/command_runtime.py artifact writer and 16 KiB event bound
acceptance_map.validation: Oversized secret fixture asserts one redacted artifact and combined event delta <=16384 bytes.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC6: A user message interrupts an active wait without terminating or duplicating the command.
acceptance_map.validation: Fake user interrupt releases wait; assert running state, unchanged handle and launch_count==1.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC7: Restarting or resuming a task reconnects to the existing command rather than executing it again.
acceptance_map.validation: Recreate runtime; assert reconnect_count==1, launch_count==1 and terminal delivery once.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC8: A validation wave with multiple processes produces no more than one ordinary completion wake-up per wave.
acceptance_map.validation: Complete three fake commands in every order; assert ordinary aggregate deliveries<=1.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC9: Hosts without native completion events use a runtime-side blocking wait, not repeated model-driven polling.
acceptance_map.validation: No-event adapter asserts one runtime wait, zero model polls and one terminal delivery.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC10: An end-to-end long-command scenario demonstrates at least a 90% reduction in polling-related tokens.
acceptance_map.validation: Run one end-to-end scenario; assert polling_token_reduction_percent>=90 against baseline.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC11: Unchanged polling turns equal zero.
acceptance_map.validation: Targeted suite and end-to-end record assert unchanged_model_polls==0.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC12: Polling-related raw tokens remain below 1% of total run tokens.
acceptance_map.validation: Frozen record asserts polling_raw_tokens/total_raw_tokens<0.01 and fails closed if unavailable.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC13: Authorization and human-input requests remain visible and cannot be suppressed by the optimization.
acceptance_map.validation: Race fixtures assert approval/input events remain visible before ordinary completion suppression.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC14: Existing timeout, cancellation, audit, and failure-reporting behavior remains fail-safe.
acceptance_map.validation: Timeout, repeated-cancel, crash/replay, lost-binding and audit fixtures assert one fail-safe terminal record and no relaunch.

risks.risk: A handle leaks identity or is replayed across workspace/auth boundaries.
risks.mitigation: Use 128-bit opaque ids, fingerprint-only metadata, and reject mismatched bindings.

risks.risk: Crash boundaries duplicate execution or delivery.
risks.mitigation: Persist launch intent/binding, use monotonic revisions and consumer leases, never auto-relaunch unverifiable bindings.

risks.risk: Host drift silently reintroduces model polling.
risks.mitigation: Normalize both adapters and prove no-event fallback with one blocking wait and zero model polls.
Prioritize approval/input/failure/timeout/cancel and suppress ordinary child completion only.

risks.risk: Telemetry becomes vanity data or leaks logs.
risks.mitigation: Hard gates, counters/hashes only, and unproven status when totals are absent.

failure_modes.detection: command_transition signal reports existing handle/revision/delivery key.
failure_modes.recovery: Runtime immediately replays the original event without new execution or wake.

failure_modes.mode: Runtime restarts with a live command.
failure_modes.detection: command_recovery signal reports a persisted running snapshot.
failure_modes.recovery: Runtime owner reconnects once; binding_lost becomes one failure and never relaunches.

failure_modes.mode: Output exceeds bounds or contains secrets.
failure_modes.detection: command_output signal reports bytes, truncation and redaction counts.
failure_modes.recovery: Artifact writer stores one redacted artifact and emits <=16 KiB plus reference.

failure_modes.detection: command_transition signal records ordered revisions and attention priority.
failure_modes.recovery: Runtime exposes attention once; wave owner suppresses only subsequent ordinary child completion.

failure_modes.detection: command_transition and wave_state signals report timed_out member.
failure_modes.recovery: Runtime cancels tree, wakes once for timeout, then emits at most one aggregate terminal event.
Observability owner blocks the efficiency gate; no pass is manufactured.

signals: command_transition signal: handle fingerprint, revision, state, wake reason, elapsed_ms and delivery disposition
command_output signal: artifact hash/reference, bytes, truncation and redaction counts
command_recovery signal: reconnect outcome, binding_lost and duplicate-launch prevention
wave_state signal: member counts, attention wakes and aggregate completion deliveries
command_efficiency signal: launches, duration, wakes, unchanged polls, avoided tokens, polling share, timeouts and cancellations
alerts: Alert on more than one terminal delivery or ordinary wave completion.
Alert on relaunch during reconnect or binding rejection.

rollout.strategy: Additive TASKPLANE_EVENT_COMMANDS flag: dual-record fake/telemetry with synchronous authority, enable evaluator/validation commands on both hosts, then waves after parity/resume proof. One deterministic repair batch and one end-to-end validation.
rollout.rollback: Disable async for new launches, retain v1 reader until handles finish/expire, finish or cancel live commands through runtime, and use synchronous wrapper for new launches; delete no state and require no simultaneous deployment.

proposed_edges.reason: Owns handles, transitions, artifacts and delivery.
Normalizes host launch, wait, cancel, reconnect and snapshot.
Persists before yield and resumes from events.
Uses canonical lifecycle on both hosts.
